html:
The Spanish-American War was a short war in 1898 in which the United States defeated Spain in Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines. It began after the battleship Maine blew up in Havana harbour in February.

In Cuba, American troops with Cuban rebels took the hills above Santiago at the Battle of San Juan Hill, and the US navy destroyed the Spanish fleet as it left Santiago harbour. The fighting lasted about ten weeks.

In the Treaty of Paris, Spain gave up Cuba and ceded Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines to the United States. For Spain it was the Disaster of 1898, the end of its empire in the Americas. For the US it was the start of an overseas empire, and for Cubans a war won by their own struggle but taken over by others.
sum: The Spanish-American War was a short war in 1898 in which the United States defeated Spain in Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines. It began after the battleship Maine blew up in Havana harbour in February.
